post.description: Checks the email and password and starts a web session: the response sets the session cookie. A session the request already carries ends. A wrong address or password answers 401, always with the same message; a body that breaks the schema answers 400, 413, 415 or 422, and no error detail echoes a value it sent. After 10 failed sign-ins in 15 minutes from one address, or for one account, sign-ins from there or for it answer 429 with Retry-After until the 15 minutes have passed; sign-ins still being checked count too. When too many passwords are being checked at once, a sign-in that waited 10 seconds answers 503 with Retry-After.

schema.description: The session cookie: __Host-tdeemon_session over HTTPS (tdeemon_session over plain HTTP), HttpOnly, SameSite=Lax, for the session's lifetime.

post.description: Logs a meal under the client's UUIDv7 (201); the same meal sent again under it is a retry (200), another a conflict (409). Without an id, from a client that cannot make one, the server makes it: that meal sent again is another, so look at get_day before sending it again. An item is a food of the user's by its food_id, or a new food, which is saved, each with a quantity in the food's unit (g or ml), servings or portions; or an estimate of a whole plate. The answer holds the meal with what each item brought, where its day stands, and warnings: values that do not add up, or a meal that looks like one logged minutes before.

200.description: The same sent again: a retry.

delete.description: Deletes a meal, and says where its day stands without it. Its id stays the deleted meal's: a meal logged under it again is refused (409).

patch.description: Changes a meal: when it was eaten, its words, and its items, by ops in order: add an item, replace one, remove one. An item no op touches keeps what it brought when logged, though its food was corrected since. An add carries its item's id, a UUID the client makes: an add of an item the meal has under its id is a retry when it is the same, a conflict (409) when not. A replace with what the item has already changes nothing, so it does not take a corrected food's values: remove the item and add it again under a new id for that. A remove of an item no longer there changes nothing.

post.description: Takes back the user's latest change not undone yet, made through any client: a meal, a food, a measurement, a check-in. Each undo takes a new UUIDv7 id: the same id sent again (a retry) answers as before, marked repeated, and takes back nothing more; without an id, from a client that cannot make one, the server makes it, and the undo sent again takes back another change; undo under a new id to go further back. Nothing is redone. Changes of the plan and an import's writes are left. A change that cannot be taken back (an import wrote over it, or what came since clashes with it) is a conflict (409) that says why, and is passed over, so the next undo takes back the change before it. The answer says what was taken back; get_day shows the day after it.
